title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 sketchbook-to-itinerary crosswalk

publication_policy.instruction: Keep sketchbook images and image-derived layer in research/backend only. Do not add sketchbook images, thumbnails, or a sketchbook layer to the public GitHub Pages map without a new explicit decision.
publication_policy.catalogue_rights_note: The Rakow catalogue labels the digital item Creative Commons No Copyright / Public Domain Mark, but this project is currently applying a deliberately more conservative frontend publication policy.

corning_record.title: R. Blaschka [sketchbook].
corning_record.creator: Rudolf Blaschka (1857-1939)
corning_record.repository: Rakow Research Library, The Corning Museum of Glass
catalogue_notes: Beginning sketch is captioned '... Tempe, Arizona, 22. April 1892'.
Most pages are blank and are not filmed.
A few pages of laid-in sketches of islands with palm trees have been included in the filming.
Digitized September 2009 by Boston Photo Imaging.
Displayed at the Rakow Research Library in 2007.

research_distinction.travel_sketchbook: Small landscape/travel sketchbook. The filmed surrogate contains desert landscapes plus a separate group of laid-in tropical harbour/island drawings.
research_distinction.botanical_study_drawings: Separate, much larger corpus catalogued primarily by plant taxon. Corning 2007 uses individual botanical studies such as Jacaranda filicifolia; these should not be conflated with pages of this travel sketchbook.
research_distinction.working_hypothesis: Synchronize landscape pages with the correspondence itinerary first; only then cross-link separately catalogued botanical studies, specimens, seeds/bulbs and finished models.

catalogue_surrogate_conflict.catalogue_claim: Beginning sketch captioned Tempe, Arizona, 22 April 1892.
catalogue_surrogate_conflict.surrogate_observation: In the supplied 30-page PDF, the earliest clearly legible landscape caption is 'Wüste bei Maricopa (Arizona) / 24. April 1892'; a second nearby caption also appears to identify a cactus-desert view at/near Maricopa on 24 April.
possible_explanations: the catalogue note refers to a physical leaf not included in the current filmed surrogate
a filmed Tempe image is missing or omitted from the PDF assembly
the catalogue description contains a metadata error
recto/verso ordering or graphite show-through complicates digital page sequence
catalogue_surrogate_conflict.guard: Do not silently replace either statement. Treat Tempe 22 April as secure correspondence chronology, but not yet as a secure sketchbook-page identification in this digital surrogate.

spatial_evidence_types.exact_point: A fixed place or infrastructure node directly secured by inscription/record.
spatial_evidence_types.field_area: A bounded locality or excursion area secured to a place/date but lacking an exact viewpoint.
spatial_evidence_types.corridor: A moving observational segment, usually rail or ship travel, for which a single point would be misleading.
spatial_evidence_types.probable_view_sector: A modeled viewpoint and direction inferred from visible landmarks; never presented as exact without independent corroboration.

page_matches.subject: broad cactus/chaparral desert plain with a continuous rugged mountain range

itinerary_match.relation: The correspondence places Rudolf in Maricopa on 24 April after the Tempe fieldwork and before the Arizona-to-California rail journey.

geolocation.primary_mountain_candidate: Sierra Estrella / Hayes Peak sector to the northwest
geolocation.alternative_mountain_candidate: Table Top Mountains sector to the south-southwest

page_matches.notes: The drawing should not be collapsed to a station marker. It records an environmental field/view area. Mountain identification remains a horizon-matching problem.

page_matches.visible_botanical_note: Opuntia bigelovii [reading high-probability; spelling reflects historic annotation]
page_matches.subject: cactus desert with tall columnar forms and a jagged mountain mass

itinerary_match.relation: Rudolf later describes the Tempe/Maricopa landscape as chaparral and cactus desert with a rocky mountain range behind it.

geolocation.alternative_mountain_candidate: Table Top Mountains or another Gila/Maricopa desert range

page_matches.subject: large steep rocky mountain rising abruptly from sparse stony desert

itinerary_match.relation: Rudolf describes the rail landscape from Arizona to Yuma, the nearly vegetationless California salt desert, the below-sea-level Salton depression, then a climb past snow-covered San Jacinto.

geolocation.primary_landform_candidate: San Jacinto massif viewed from the Colorado/Coachella desert rail corridor
geolocation.alternative: another rocky range on the Maricopa-Yuma-California transit segment

page_matches.guard: Do not assign a point or date until an inscription, railway milepoint, or stronger silhouette match is found.

page_matches.caption_transcription: [probable] Wüste bei Hesperia ... [probable date line: 5 May 1892]
page_matches.subject: tree-like yucca/Joshua-tree desert with high mountain chain behind

itinerary_match.archive_anchor: retrospective account in Agua Caliente letter, 7 May 1892
itinerary_match.relation: The letter says they arrived at Hesperia about 3 a.m., stayed at a hotel near the station, and at daybreak saw a vast desert plain surrounded by mountains, with tree-like Yucca brevifolia rising 'like a forest' and a snow-topped San Bernardino summit behind.

geolocation.probable_view_direction: southeast toward the San Bernardino high peaks

page_matches.notes: This is a strong image-text match and should be added to the research itinerary as a 5 May field node. The public map is intentionally unchanged in this pass.

page_matches.subject: tropical harbour or lagoon with buildings on a palm-covered shore, small palm island and mountains behind

itinerary_match.archive_anchor: BLA-D00736 · 017:90 and related retrospective Jamaica correspondence
itinerary_match.relation: Rudolf landed at Port Antonio on 28 February and later wrote specifically about his impressions of Port Antonio while travelling onward aboard Bowden.

geolocation.candidate: Port Antonio harbour / Navy Island group

page_matches.subject: striped lighthouse on a low point at left, palm-covered island/shore at right, harbour water and mountainous interior behind

itinerary_match.relation: The Port Antonio landing and immediate onward coastal voyage create a plausible shipboard context for a harbour-approach sketch.

geolocation.modeled_view: offshore north of Port Antonio, facing generally south into the harbour; Folly Point would fall east/left and Navy Island west/right

page_matches.guard: Landmark configuration is a geospatial inference, not an inscription. Preserve as probable until checked against a historical harbour chart/coastal profile and additional period images.

page_matches.subject: close tropical waterway/harbour edge with dense palms

itinerary_match.candidate: same Jamaica / Port Antonio laid-in group as pages 21 and 23

geolocation.candidate: Port Antonio harbour or nearby north-coast Jamaican inlet

unmatched_secure_correspondence_events.evidence: Wagon excursion a few miles outside Tempe; cactus flowers drawn; live cacti collected; Delphinium drawn after return.
unmatched_secure_correspondence_events.sketchbook_status: No filmed page in the supplied 30-page PDF has yet been securely identified as the catalogue's Tempe 22 April beginning sketch.

next_actions: Compare pages 5 and 9 against Sierra Estrella and Table Top horizon profiles from plausible Maricopa viewpoints.
Use the circa-1890/1891 Huntington Hesperia townsite maps to recover the depot/hotel area, then test the page-17 mountain bearing toward the San Bernardino high peaks.
Use a Port Antonio harbour chart and landmark geometry to constrain the page-23 shipboard view sector; treat pages 21 and 25 as associated only if topology remains consistent.
Inspect the 30 individual Rakow JPG delivery files if available; they may preserve more graphite detail than the assembled PDF.
Keep all sketchbook imagery and image-derived map layers backend-only during this phase.
